postTitle: What-If Scenarios: Test a Decision Before You Make It
topic: Change one thing at a time: a move that adds €200 a month hides a €600 gain and a €400 loss

assumptions.notes: Eva saves €1,000 a month: €4,000 pay after tax minus €3,000 costs. Job offer in a cheaper city: pay 10% lower (€3,600), costs 20% lower (€2,400). Pay cut alone: €3,600 minus €3,000 = €600 (€400 less). Cheaper city alone: €4,000 minus €2,400 = €1,600 (€600 more). Both: €3,600 minus €2,400 = €1,200 (€200 more). The 10% and 20% are illustrative inputs, not claims about any real city.

hookVariants.narration: Before you decide on a big change, split it into its parts.

beats.narration: Eva saves a thousand euros a month. Four thousand in, three thousand out.
She is offered a job in a cheaper city. It pays ten percent less. On its own, that pay cut leaves her six hundred a month.
On its own, the cheaper city cuts her costs by a fifth. That leaves sixteen hundred a month.
Together, twelve hundred. Only two hundred more than today.
The total hides what is doing the work. The city is a big gain. The pay cut takes most of it back.
So test one change at a time. Run each change alone, then all of them together. Then compare which one does the work.
